Spotify Songs' Genre Segmentation

1. Data pre-processing

  • Raw shape: (32833, 23)
  • Missing values: 15 (all in track_name / artist / album of 5 rows)
  • After dropping null rows: 32828
  • Rows sharing a track_id (same song listed in several playlists): 4476
  • Unique songs used for modelling: 28352

    • Features were standardised (zero mean, unit variance). Right-skewed features (speechiness, instrumentalness, liveness) were log1p-transformed first so a few extreme values don't dominate the distance.

    3. Correlation matrix

    Correlation of features

    Strongest positive: loudness / energy (0.68). Strongest negative: acousticness / energy (-0.55), and acousticness / loudness (-0.37). Energy, loudness and acousticness carry overlapping information.

    4. Clustering

    Choosing k

    Silhouette scores are low across all k (best 0.18), meaning songs form a continuous spectrum rather than tight separate blobs. k = 6 was used so the clusters can be compared directly against the 6 playlist genres.

    Cluster vs playlist_genre

    Adjusted Rand Index vs playlist genre: 0.066 (0 = random, 1 = identical). Audio features alone only partly recover genre — EDM (cluster 2) and rap (cluster 5) are the only genres that form a clear majority in a cluster; pop, r&b, latin and rock are spread across several clusters and overlap heavily.

    Clusters by sub-genre

    Clusters by playlist name

    Playlist-level clustering ARI vs genre: 0.299 — averaging over a playlist removes noise, so playlists group by genre much more cleanly than individual songs.

    5. Model & recommendation system

    Supervised check: a random forest predicts playlist genre from audio features with 56.1% test accuracy (chance ≈ 17%). Top features: tempo, speechiness, danceability, energy.

    Recommender: given a song, find its cluster, then rank the other songs in that cluster by cosine similarity of their scaled audio features.

    Sanity check on 300 random songs: on average 40% of the top-10 recommendations share the seed song's genre (random baseline ≈ 17%).

    Key takeaways

  • Songs form a continuous spectrum; clustering is soft and genres overlap, especially pop / r&b / latin.
  • Energy–loudness are strongly positively correlated; acousticness is negatively correlated with both.
  • EDM has the highest energy and tempo, rap the highest speechiness and danceability, r&b the lowest energy and highest acousticness, rock the lowest danceability.
  • Playlist-level averages cluster cleanly by genre; individual songs are noisier.
  • Cluster + cosine similarity gives a working content-based recommender; add popularity or artist filters to improve it.
